title: LIGHTS ON — Claude Opus 5.5 launch trailer (2:13.6)
logline: In a cathedral-sized dark hall one cursor learns to code, and within ≈5 months a demo becomes a budget line. Then the camera pulls back: code was one lit box on a dark delivery line. Work piles into towers, flat agent swarms make it worse, and the hall goes silent until someone asks who runs the line. The factory's lights come on bank by bank, graph, hierarchy and swarm lock into place, and a foreman rises at the centre of it: Claude Opus 5.5. The clock starts again.
spine: Code is the station everyone watches: one clay cursor glows in a vast dark hall.
BUT in Oct 2025 the verdict on agents was "they just don't work."
BUT on Nov 24 2025 Opus 4.5 shipped, THEREFORE within ≈5 months capability became budget (run-rate ~$9B → $30B+, Anthropic-reported).
BUT writing code is only 16% of a developer's time. The blazing code station turns out to be one lit box on a long dark line.
THEREFORE work coming out of code at agent speed piles up at stations still running at human speed (review, test, deploy), and THE LINE WAITS.
THEREFORE the reflex is to add more agents, BUT independent agents amplify errors ×17.2 and the flat swarm jams the line.
THEREFORE the real question surfaces in silence: who runs the line?
The answer is structure, the SOFTWARE FACTORY: graph for control, hierarchy for coherence, swarm for parallel work. With a coordinator, error amplification falls to ×4.4.
THEREFORE the line needs a foreman: 100-agent teams that self-organize, one session directing a dozen, 18+ hours unattended, Fable 5.1-level work at 40% lower cost. That foreman is Claude Opus 5.5.
THEREFORE the clock restarts at MONTH 1. If the pattern holds, budgets come in early 2027 (labelled as a projection).
motifs: M1 THE CLAY SPARK (protagonist; cursor ▮ → orb → foreman core). Act I: a lone clay cursor block blinks on the tick at a single station, then ignites as an orb that writes code (it is ≤2% of the frame and the only warm object). Act II: it is lost and dimmed inside a cold flat swarm. Act III: it is the core at the apex of the hierarchy, with threads running to every station. Button: alone again in the Act I composition, now with the whole hall lighting behind it. It blinks on the music tick every time it appears.

M2 THE LINE (stations + refrain). Midpoint: one lit box on a dark 7-station line (top-down). Act II: the same stations jammed, work cards stacked into 300u towers under red alarm pinpoints, with the refrain THE LINE WAITS. shown twice in the same font and screen position. Turn: 8 light banks switch on one per beat. Act III: identical compositions return flowing L→R (REVIEW./TEST./DEPLOY. go from red to white), the refrain flips to THE LINE RUNS., and the top-down of the cold open pays off.

M3 THE CLOCK (tick + MONTH counter). A quarter-note tick under Act I becomes accelerating Risset ticks through MONTH 1→5 brass gates. It survives every music stop (midpoint, drop). It returns alone at 120 BPM in the button, where the counter flips MONTH 0 → MONTH 1, so the '5 months' reads as a threat that is starting again.

Supporting device: the tiny human silhouette (1.8u) as the scale reference. It stands at the one station (I), is dwarfed under the card tower in red (II), stands lit at the foreman's foot (III), and is recalled amber in the peak.
music_plan:
One timeline.json cue list drives both audio and picture. Key D minor over a D pedal; recurring 5-note motif D–F–A–G–F. Tempo is 120 BPM (beat 0.5 s) from 0:00 to 1:26, lifts to 150 BPM (beat 0.4 s, bar 1.6 s) from 1:26.0 to 2:03.6, and returns to 120 BPM for the button and end, so the clock tick comes back at its original rate. Engine sections: cold 0–8 | act1 8–38 | turn 38–44 | act2 44–82 | turn 82–89.2 | act3 89.2–110 | peak 110–118 | end 118.8–133.6.

COLD 0:00–0:08: on f0, impact + sub + tick; 8th-note preview pulse; riser 0.5→2.0 with a suckback ending exactly at 2.0; BRAAM #1 at 2.0 (D1, −2 st droop) + sub drop + impact; tom+metal hit and D6 ping at 4.0; reverse swell 5.5→6.0; at 6.0 a tape-stop rewind (−1 octave over 0.7 s); a lone tick at 7.5; 8 f black breath.

ACT I 0:08–0:38 (act1): D–A drone with an Eb Phrygian neighbour; quarter tick on every beat (the clock spine); Shepard bed at 0.08 oct/s, −28 dB; ping under cards; soft low hit every 2 bars. 14.0 gate impact. 14.5 motif statement #1 on a lone soft synth. 16.0–28.0: Risset ticks accelerate (−20 → −12 dB) under the MONTH gates; a whoosh peaks on each gate pass (16.0 / 20.0 / 23.0 / 25.5 / 27.5); data-chirp density doubles at each gate. 28.0: 2 s column riser. 30.0: impact A + sub (CAPABILITY → BUDGET). 30–37.5: groove with hits every 2 beats. 37.5: suckback ends 38.0.

SILENCE #1 38.0–38.5: digital zero, tails gated.

MIDPOINT 38.5–44 (turn): the tick alone over a D drone (about −30 LUFS-S); low hit + ping at 41.5; 1-bar noise riser 42.0, hard cut at 43.9.

MOOD CHANGE #1 at 44.0 (act2): BOOM + pulse ostinato in 8ths 'x..x..x.x..x..x.', Dm–Bb–C–Dm at 2 bars each, hit on every bar downbeat. Tricolon hits escalate: 48.0 tom / 50.0 tom+metal / 52.0 tom+metal+sub. 54.0 crash. 55.0 three pager pings. Heartbeat at 60 BPM from 56.5, doubling to 120 at 67.0. 60.0: pulse moves to 16ths (3+3+2). Glitch bursts at 63.5 / 64.0 / 69.0 / 75.0 (4 in total). Shepard bed rises to −18 dB. 71.5: low-pass + tape-stop slice, then a reverse whoosh.

ACCELERANDO 74–82: tom/kick on every cut (1.0 → 0.5 → 0.25 s); Shepard at 0.33 oct/s + an 8 s noise riser; 80.0 glitch roll 1/16 → 1/32 → 1/64; the riser peak is hard-cut at 81.95.

SILENCE #2 82.0–83.0 (the drop). 83.0 single tick; typing clicks; sub thumps at 84.5 and 85.0; 0.75 s suckback ends 86.0.

TEMPO LIFT 86.0: 8 metallic bank clunks on the beats 86.0–88.8, each pitched −2 st lower and bigger, over a 3.2 s riser + Dm string swell; pre-hit dip on the last 8th.

MOOD CHANGE #2 at 89.2 (act3): BRAAM #2 (D1) + impact + sub drop + climax theme: 16th ostinato, choir-like pads, Bb → D major lift; hits on beats 1 and 3. Structure tricolon hits at 92.4 / 94.0 / 95.6 add a layer each. 97.2: hit A. Mirror labels get click / clunk / chime at 98.8 / 99.2 / 99.6. 100.0: 0.4 s dip to pad only. 100.4: light with NO sound. 100.8: tier-S impact + sub drop (delayed boom, not a braam) + motif statement #2 on full brass pad; swell 101.6–103.6.

PROOFS 103.6–113.2: impact A on each card, alternating metal 310 / 370 Hz; data chirps under every fleet.

PEAK 113.2–117.6 (peak): a hit on every beat, 8ths from 116.4; Shepard at 0.5 oct/s + a 4 s noise riser + snare roll; tape stop on the last 8th; suckback ends at 118.0.

SILENCE #3 118.0–118.8 (false stop).

118.8: BRAAM #3, a D1+A1 power chord with no third, + impact at 0 dB + sub drop + D add9 logo shimmer; 6 s tail, left unresolved.

BUTTON (120 BPM) from 123.6: the tick returns alone at −26 dB on every beat; ping at 123.6; motif statement #3 as a single high piano line; at 128.1 a final micro-sting (chirp burst + impact −12 + ping) lands on 'BUDGETS IN EARLY 2027.'; ring-out from 129.6; pad tail 130.6–133.6 decays below −60 dBFS.

BUDGET: braams 3 (2.0, 89.2, 118.8); silences 3 (0.5 s, 1.0 s, 0.8 s); mood changes 2 + 1 tempo lift. Loudness: Act I about −22 → Act II −16 → Act III −11 LUFS-S → title momentary max −7; master −14 LUFS-I, ≤ −1 dBTP.

acts.name: COLD OPEN — flash-forward + rewind
acts.purpose: Show the lit factory first: degraded, out of context and too fast to spend. Pose the thesis number and open L1 ('the next one?'), then rewind the lights to darkness.
acts.grade: Warm but withheld: fog ×2, exposure −1 stop, sat 0.9, clay ≤10%. The rewind drains to cold steel.

acts.name: ACT I — ONE STATION (the first wave)
acts.purpose: A single cursor in a vast dark hall. Agents don't work, then Opus 4.5 ships, then MONTH 1→5 gates accelerate to a budget. Capability becomes budget. ASL 1.2 s (2.0 s shots slowing to 0.5 s).
acts.grade: Cold: void #050506, steel #5B7A93, ice; sat 0.8. Clay is the ONLY warm hue (≤2% of frame, rising to about 5% as the code tower blazes). Handheld 0.3°, Dutch 6–10°.

acts.name: MIDPOINT — code was one station
acts.purpose: The 'those aren't mountains' re-read. One 3.5 s pull-back to a top-down view: the blazing station is one lit box on a dark 7-station line. Coding is 16% of dev time.
acts.grade: Near-black, cold; one clay segment = 16% of the line length.

acts.name: ACT II — THE JAMMED LINE
acts.purpose: Make the antagonist physical: queues become towers under red pinpoints, and a tiny human is dwarfed. Refrain THE LINE WAITS. ×2. 'Just add more agents' leads to a flat swarm, collisions and errors ×17.2, then an accelerando into the drop. ASL 1.2 s → 0.25 s.
acts.grade: Cold desaturated (sat 0.75), ice whites, alert red #FF453A only as pinpoints (≤1%), clay protagonist dimmed to 30%. Dutch ±8–12°, handheld.

acts.name: THE DROP — who runs the line?
acts.purpose: Valence low point: black, 1 s of true silence, then one typed question. Opens L3.

acts.name: ACT III — LIGHTS ON (the software factory + the foreman)
acts.purpose: At 150 BPM: banks ignite one per beat → BRAAM #2 + the refrain flips to THE LINE RUNS. → THE SOFTWARE FACTORY → graph/hierarchy/swarm click in → ×17.2 → ×4.4 → mirror tour → foreman reveal (low-angle monument) → 4 sourced proofs → peak with bookend recall → suckback. ASL 0.74 s.
acts.grade: Warm: clay #D97757 / ember / brass / ivory #FAF9F5, sat 1.05. Clay 5–10% of frame, rising to 20% on the foreman. Zero handheld, level horizons, symmetry, L→R flow.
acts.letterbox: Snaps open from 2.39 to 1.78 (0 px) on the 89.2 braam frame; full frame after that.

acts.name: FALSE STOP + TITLE
acts.purpose: 0.8 s black silence, then BRAAM #3 lands with the title CLAUDE OPUS 5.5. Title at 88.9% of runtime, held ≤5 s.
acts.grade: Black ground, clay → ivory light-line, brass sweep; clay ≤20%.

acts.name: BUTTON — MONTH 1
acts.purpose: Callback plus hook. The Act I hall composition returns at eye level, calm, with the tick back. MONTH 0 → MONTH 1, the hall ignites, and the labelled projection lands on the final hit. Leaves L4 open.
acts.grade: Void + clay, then a warm radial ignition.

acts.name: END CARD — the wink
acts.purpose: A true credit that proves the thesis: this film was made by Opus 5.5 agents from one brief. Only fade in the film (last 15 f).

why_it_works:
**Story.** The film is a 10-link BUT/THEREFORE chain with no AND-THEN links. It turns the client's argument into one physical place, a cathedral-scale hall.
- Act I is the first wave on a single station.
- The midpoint pull-back reframes the whole act: code was one box (16%).
- Act II makes the abstract antagonist physical: towers, red pinpoints, a dwarfed human, and the flat swarm that makes it worse.
- The drop asks the only question left.
- Act III answers it with structure (graph, hierarchy, swarm), then with a foreman.

Proof follows the answer. The product name is withheld until 88.9% of runtime: '5.5' appears only as an engraving fragment at 75%. The capability is never withheld.

**Craft numbers (all within the bible's rules).**
- Runtime 2:13.6, 126 shots.
- ASL by act: cold open 1.0 s, Act I 1.2 s, midpoint 3.0 s (the sanctioned pull-back), Act II 0.93 s (1.2 s before the accelerando, then a halving staircase 1.0/0.5/0.25), Act III 0.74 s (peak 0.4 → 0.2 s).
- Tempo lifts from 120 to 150 BPM at the turn, so escalation is felt.
- Effects budget: 3 braams (2.0, 89.2, 118.8); 3 silences (0.5, 1.0, 0.8 s); 7 flashes; 4 glitches, all in Act II; at most 8 shakes.
- The global peak is 113.2–117.6 (85–88%), then the false stop, a 4.8 s title and a 7 s button. The music stays unresolved.

**Angle grammar has meaning.**
- Worm's-eye = threat in Act II (towers), then awe in Act III (the foreman).
- Top-down = understanding: the midpoint, the factory reveal and the graph.
- Macro = intimacy with the spark.
- The camera itself changes: handheld and Dutch in the problem acts, then on the braam the Dutch tilt rights to 0 and the horizon stays level.

**Mirror callbacks for a smart audience.** Each problem composition returns transformed:
- shot 38 → 82 (THE LINE WAITS → THE LINE RUNS, same slot and font)
- 39/41/43 → 91/92/93 (red REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY become white and flowing)
- 53 → 90 (×17.2 → ×4.4, same lens)
- hold #2 → 113 (the human under a lit tower)
- cold-open shots 1/2/4 → 108–110 (bookend, now warm)
- Act I hall → button

**Copy and claims.**
- Every card is also a visual event: stamped on stations, engraved, in world space, a counter rolling on a hit, or typed in-scene.
- 137 on-screen words (cap 140), at most 7 words per card, about 34% of runtime with text.
- Every number is from facts.md, shortened and never strengthened. Vendor and customer claims carry a source whisper (ANTHROPIC-REPORTED, SYSTEM CARD, STRIPE, CLIO, ANTHROPIC, GOOGLE RESEARCH, ATLASSIAN).
- The 2027 line is labelled IF THE PATTERN HOLDS + PROJECTION.
- The end credit is a true wink: the film was made by the factory it sells.

**Buildable with the engine.** Every set piece is a primitive or particle field in the kit:
- pillars, stations, cards and gates are glowBox
- agents are orb or instanced spheres (at most 2,000 per shot); counts beyond that are particles (at most 30k)
- light banks and alarm beams are beam
- graph edges and threads are fatLine
- the human is a black capsule-plus-sphere silhouette with rim light
- engraved type is textPlane
- the title forge is 2D
- the drop, false stop and end card are about 10× cheaper type-on-black shots.
risks: Word budget is at 137/140. Adding any source tag or date will break the cap, so cut elsewhere first (e.g. the 7 midpoint station labels can drop DESIGN/OPERATE).

The 2027 card must never appear without 'IF THE PATTERN HOLDS:' and the 'PROJECTION' whisper. The cold open deliberately ASKS 'THE NEXT ONE?' instead of claiming the next wave has started, because 'the next wave has started' is client framing that facts.md does not support.

'100-AGENT TEAMS, SELF-ORGANIZED.' paraphrases 'picked their own structure' (system card). If legal wants verbatim wording, use 'PICKED THEIR OWN STRUCTURE' and cut 3 words elsewhere. Never imply Opus 5.5 is Anthropic's most capable or 'best'. Avoid hype words.

The run-rate (~$9B → $30B+) is company-wide and Anthropic-reported, not coding-only revenue. Its whisper tag must stay legible (≥22 px) and the card must sit at MONTH 5, so it is read as the end-2025 → Apr 2026 change.
The 16% visual is a share of developer TIME shown as line length. It must not read as '16% of stations'; keep the sweep proportional to length and the card wording as written.
The $285B rout / 'SaaSpocalypse' is deliberately excluded: it was triggered by a legal tool, and showing it inside the coding story would mislead.

The tempo lift needs per-section BPM in the audio renderer. engine beats() is fixed at 120, so Act III and title durations must be written in seconds (0.4 s grid) and verified against the cue list frame by frame. The return to 120 BPM at 123.6 also needs a clean splice.

Photosensitivity: the Act II accelerando (0.25 s) and Act III recall flurry (0.2 s) must be luminance-matched within ±8%, never alternate image and black, and contain no saturated-red full-field frames. Run an automated flash check of at most 3 per 30 f window.

Render time is about 1.6 h for roughly 120 s of 3D. Swarm and rail shots must stay ≤30k particles and ≤2,000 instances; the 1,000 rails and 4,096 cursors must use instancing (or a particle sprite for the cursors).

The bookend shots (108–110) and mirror shots (82, 90–93, 111, 113) must reuse the exact camera functions of their source shots, via a shared module. Otherwise the payoff reads as a near-miss rather than a callback.
Holds over 3 s: the midpoint pull-back (3.5 s), the drop (4.0 s, a black type shot) and the title (4.8 s). Keep internal events every ≤2 s in each (label decodes, tick, typed characters, sub thumps).
